```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is narrow: one paying customer within 90 days. Idea A is a self-serve App Store subscription at $3.99–$4.99/month, anchored to Bulletin's live pricing. Solo developers have already shipped and monetized near-identical apps (Bulletin, Syft, KhanList, Content Bite), so a first paid conversion through IAP needs no sales cycle, contracts or integration work.",
    "Idea B's own brief documents a near-identical precedent, Cydoc. It had an MD/PhD founder and ran for seven years, yet reached only four paying customers and $27,900 in 2024 revenue. It faced $4,000–$6,000 per-practice integration costs and customers who wanted to renegotiate scope per practice. That points to a slow, custom sales cycle that does not fit a 90-day window.",
    "Idea B needs a HIPAA BAA executed with every customer, ongoing safeguards, and an FDA non-device legal review before it can take sensitive data. Its cited channel, conference exhibiting at $3,000–$10,000 per booth, is costly and slow for a solo operator. Idea A's regulatory load is a one-time IP consult plus platform self-declaration forms.",
    "Idea A's strongest counter-evidence, Artifact's shutdown and a saturated free/freemium field, mainly threatens sustained scale and retention. It does not threaten getting a first paying user, which is the stated bar. Idea B's counter-evidence threatens the first sale itself.",
    "Idea B has better unit economics on paper ($49–$99/provider/month versus about $4/month). But the brief gives no evidence that a solo builder without clinical credentials can close even one practice faster than Cydoc did."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's main direct demand quote comes from a PMHNP who is an employee, not a practice owner. She says her employer ignored her request for more pre-intake paperwork. That shows workflow frustration, not willingness to pay for an AI intake or note tool, and it does not come from the stated payer. The other demand point, '1 in 5 physicians spend 8+ hours/week in the EHR', is AMA data relayed second-hand through a competitor's marketing page.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs are weak on demand. Idea A's willingness-to-pay evidence is one conditional app-store review ('Revert the UI back and I'll pay'), and nothing shows that indie organic launches converted. The decision rests on fit with the 90-day first-customer goal: friction, sales cycle and regulatory overhead clearly favor A. If the question were long-term viability or revenue per customer, the call would be much closer and might flip."
}
```
